title: The Phoenix Lights Incident
hook: On March 13, 1997, thousands in Phoenix, Arizona saw a massive V-shaped formation of lights that vanished.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: At 7:30 p.m., orange and white lights stretched over 300 m across the sky.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The Air Force said they were flares dropped from aircraft at Barry Goldwater Range.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: More than 400 witnesses, including a news crew, filmed the silent V formation.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Airport radar recorded objects at an altitude of 3,000 ft moving rapidly at the same time.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Scientists propose theories from secret aircraft to plasma, but no agreement.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: A 2017 declassified file notes a flare test over the Phoenix zone, yet the pattern differed from the observed V.

end.line: What really lit the Phoenix night sky?

description: A brief look at the 1997 Phoenix Lights and the unanswered questions.

facts.claim: The Phoenix Lights were observed on March 13, 1997, around 7:30 p.m.
The U.S. Air Force later explained the lights as flares dropped during a training exercise at Barry Goldwater Range.
More than 400 people, including a local news crew, reported seeing the V-shaped lights.
Airport radar at Phoenix Sky Harbor logged unidentified objects at an altitude of about 3,000 ft during the event.
A declassified 2017 document revealed a test of infrared counter-measure flares over the Phoenix area that night.
